91: RoleAssignments = new Mongo.Collection("roleAssignments");
92: // Edges in the permissions sharing graph.
93: //
94: // To share a permission with another user is to declare "if I have this permission, then so should
95: // the recipient". A bundle of such declarations by a single sharer directed at a single recipient
96: // for a single grain is called a "role assignment". A grain's owner always has every permission,
97: // but permissions for other users must be computed from this collection.
98: //
99: // Any grain for which a user has received a role assignment should show up in that user's grain
100: // list. However, the user may only access a grain if there is a path of *active* role assignments
101: // leading from the grain owner to that user, precisely as if every role assignment carried a
102: // special "can open grain" permission.
103: //
104: // Each contains:
105: //   _id: random
106: //   grainId: The `_id` of the grain whose permissions are being shared.
107: //   sharer: The `_id` of the user who is sharing these permissions.
108: //   recipient: The `_id` of the user who receives these permissions.
109: //   roleAssignment: A JSON-encoded Grain.ViewSharingLink.RoleAssignment representing the
110: //                   received permissions. The sharer is allowed to modify this later.
111: //   active: Flag indicating that this role assignment has not been revoked. The sharer is allowed
112: //           to flip this bit, but only the recipient is allowed to delete the role assignment.
113: //   petname: Human-readable label chosen by and only visible to the sharer.
114: //   title: Human-readable title as chosen by the recipient. Used in the same places that
115: //          `grain.title` is used for the grain's owner.
116: //   created: Date when this role assignment was created.
117: //   parent: If present, the `_id` of the entry in ApiTokens from which this was derived.

196: // now they are also used to implement SturdyRefs, not just held by external users, but also when
197: // an app holds a SturdyRef to another app within the same server. See the various `save()`,
198: // `restore()`, and `drop()` methods in `grain.capnp` (on `SansdtormApi`, `AppPersistent`, and
199: // `MainView`) -- the fields of type `Data` are API tokens.

201: // Each contains:
202: //   _id:       A SHA-256 hash of the token.
203: //   grainId:   The grain servicing this API. (Not present if the API isn't serviced by a grain.)
204: //   userId:    The `_id` of the user (in the users table) to whom this token should be attributed.
205: //              The user's current permissions will be presented to the app whenever the token is
206: //              restored, so that the app can limit the token to the user's permissions, especially
207: //              if they have changed. `userId` is not present if `userInfo` is present.
208: //   userInfo:  For API tokens created by the app through HackSessionContext, the UserInfo struct
209: //              that should be passed to `newSession()` when exercising this token, in decoded (JS
210: //              object) format. This is a temporary hack.
211: //   roleAssignment: If this API token represents a UiView, this field contains a JSON-encoded
212: //              Grain.ViewSharingLink.RoleAssignment representing the permissions it carries. These
213: //              permissions will be intersected with those held by `userId` when the view is opened.
214: //   forSharing: If true, requests sent to the HTTP API endpoint with this token will be treated as
215: //              anonymous rather than as directly associated with `userId`. This has no effect on
216: //              the permissions granted.
217: //   objectId:  If present, this token represents an arbitrary Cap'n Proto capability exported by
218: //              the app or its supervisor (whereas without this it strictly represents UiView).
219: //              sturdyRef is the JSON-encoded SupervisorObjectId (defined in `supervisor.capnp`).
220: //              Note that if the SupervisorObjectId contains an AppObjectId, that field is
221: //              treated as type AnyPointer, and so encoded as a raw Cap'n Proto message.
222: //   frontendRef: If present, this token actually refers to an object implemented by the front-end,
